subject: Chemistry
title: Particle Accelerators Make Elements
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Particle Accelerators Make Elements.

hook.text: To create a new element, scientists smash atoms together at millions of miles per hour and hope they stick.

buildup.text: A particle accelerator fires ions at a target foil for weeks or months. Most collisions fail completely.

discovery.text: Occasionally, two nuclei fuse into one heavier nucleus. Detectors catch the new atom before it decays.

twist.text: Some experiments run for years to produce a single atom. Element 117 required 6 months of continuous bombardment.

climax.text: Labs in Russia, Germany, Japan, and the US compete to reach new elements. It's the modern gold rush.

punchline.text: Millions of collisions for one atom. Patience makes elements.

quiz.question: How are superheavy elements typically created?
options: By smashing atomic nuclei together in particle accelerators
By cooling gases to absolute zero

details.summary: Since 1940, particle accelerators have been used to create all transuranium elements by smashing lighter nuclei together at tremendous speeds..
details.whyItMatters: Particle accelerators extended the periodic table to 118 elements, testing the limits of nuclear stability. Creating superheavy elements probes fundamental physics about whether atoms can exist beyond certain limits.
takeaways: All elements beyond uranium were created using particle accelerators
Superheavy elements are produced one atom at a time from heavy ion collisions
Creating element 118 required months of bombardment to produce just a few atoms

faq.question: How do particle accelerators create new elements?
faq.answer: Accelerators propel ions of one element to extremely high speeds and slam them into a target of another element. Occasionally, two nuclei merge instead of shattering, forming a heavier nucleus with a combined proton count..

faq.question: Why is creating superheavy elements becoming increasingly difficult?
faq.answer: As elements get heavier, the repulsive force between protons makes nuclei increasingly unstable. The probability of two heavy nuclei fusing successfully drops dramatically, requiring months of continuous bombardment to produce a single atom..
